name: SikaTile-350 Pro Maxset
paste:
SIKATILE®-350 PRO MAXSET: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset, March 2025, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sikatile-350-promaxset.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (March 2025, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is an economic polymer fortified cement-based tile and stone adhesive with Dust Less technology which reduces airborne dust in the mixing phase by up to 80%.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is available in both white or grey.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset white is free from respirable crystalline silica.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is suitable for internal and external applications on both walls and floors. Suitable Tile Types include;
    - Ceramic Tiles
    - Porcelain tiles
    - Natural Stone* including marble and granite etc
    - Engineered stone / Man made stone*
    - Concrete, (concrete greater than 35 MPa shall be mechanically prepared).
    - Cement boards and sheets*
    - Cement renders and screeds, including early ageds screeds
    - Rendered block and brickwork
    - Light weight construction boards coated with cement coatings
    - Under tile Sika waterproofing membranes
    - Gypsum Plasterboard
    - Tile on Tile applications when used with SikaTile 015 Prep n Prime
    *Not suitable for use with tile and stone sensitive to moisture/water.
    Suitable Substrates Include;
    *Refer to board manufacturers strict installation instructions for details and load limits.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: A FLEXIBLE CEMENT-BASED TILE ADHESIVE WITH DUST LESS TECHNOLOGY DESIGN FOR LARGE FORMAT TILE INSTALLATIONS
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (March 2025, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS ISO 13007: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - AS3958:2023: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Ecology, Health And Safety > SUBSTRATE QUALITY (p.3).
    - AS 3958:2023: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Ecology, Health And Safety > APPLICATION (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Equipped with DUST LESS Technology
    - High bond strength
    - Economical
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset white is free from Respirable Crystalline Silca
    - Flexible S1 performance
    - Excellent non slump suitable for large format
    - Excellent workability
    - Available in both white and grey finishes
    - Low VOC
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Colour: Manufactured on both Grey and white cement (Sand source may affect final colour)
    - Product declaration: C2TES1 as per AS ISO 13007.
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20kg bags / 64 bags per pallet
    - Shelf life: If unopened 12 months from date of manufacture.
    - Storage conditions: Store off ground in dry cool conditions. (High humidity will reduce shelf life).

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (March 2025, Version 01.01) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (March 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Pot Life: 2 hours at 23°C & 50% relative humidity.
    - Open Time: 30 minutes at 23°C & 50% relative humidity
4.3 Consumption.
    | Notched trowel size | Approx coverage per bag |
    | 6mm notched trowel | 11m² |
    | 10mm Notched trowel | 6m² |
    Consumption is always dependant on the substrate surface profile, roughness and application technique.
4.4 Applied product ready for use.
    | USE | WAIT TIME |
    | Prior to grouting | 24 hours |
    | Dry area use | 48 hours |
    | Wet area use | 7 days |
    Application imformation values determined at laboratory conditions: 23°C, & 50% RH. Higher temperatures will reduce wait times and lower with increase. High humidity will prolong setting times.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable for applications over tongue and grooved timber flooring, plywood, medium density fibre board, or Masonite.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable for moisture sensitive stone use SikaTile 440 Opti-Cure
    - For applications externally above 3 meters use in conjunction with mechanical fixing / shelfing systems.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable to be applied directly over solvent based waterproof membranes.
    - The performance of cement based adhesives will be compromised when used above 35°C and under 5°C.
    - Efflorescence is beyond the control of the manufacturer due to external influences beyond our control
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable for submersed applications.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable for direct tile over tile applications. Use SikaTile 015 Prep n Prime prior to tiling.
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable for heavy duty applications such as vehicular traffic.
    - During curing ensure protection from extreme heat, extreme sunlight, & water ingress.
    - Contact Sika Australia for advice if further information is required.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations. It is essential to plan the area to be tiled, with the inclusionof movement joints, in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards. Failure to do so may result in drummy or lifting tiles. Make sure normal building or surface movement is accommodated by installing movement joints as follows:
    - Over movement joints in the substrate
    - At a junction between different substrate materials
    - At fixtures interrupting the tile surface e.g. columns
    - At internal vertical corners
    - Around the perimeter of the tiling system
    - At a maximum of 4.5m centres, in a grid pattern Movement joints should be kept free from dirt and adhesive
    - All movement joints can be filled with a suitable Sika sealant and suitable backing rod or backing tape

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.5):
    - SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset is not suitable for moisture sensitive stone use SikaTile 440 Opti-Cure
    - The performance of cement based adhesives will be compromised when used above 35°C and under 5°C.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset, March 2025, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sikatile-350-promaxset.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaTile 350 Pro Maxset - Grey, version 19/03/2024, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/MSDS%20SikaTile-350%20PRO%20Maxset%20Grey%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaTile 350 PRO Maxset - White, version 30/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/MSDS%20SikaTile-350%20PRO%20Maxset%20White%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset, version 24/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/sds-sikatile-350promaxset.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset, version 24/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sds-sikatile-350promaxset.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Equipment.
    - Personal protective equipment
    - Mixing drill with stirring attachment
    - Clean mixing buckets
    - Trowels
6.4 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality. All surfaces must be installed according to manufacturer’s instructions and relevant Australian Standard(s) and be structurally sound, dry, clean and free from movement, oil, grease, wax, sealers, curing compounds, release agents and any other loose or contaminating material. Thoroughly clean old surfaces, or new surfaces that have been treated, prior to tiling. Deeply contaminated surfaces must be prepared/abraded to a clean, sound surface. Expose at least 80% of the original substrate of painted surfaces. Substrates shall meet relevant deflection standards outlined in the relevant Australian Standards (AS3958:2023).
6.5 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality - Concrete substrates. New concrete shall be 7 days old and be left with a wood float finish. Steel trowel finished concrete is generally acceptable if the concrete allows water penetration. Concrete above 35MPa shall be mechanically prepared.
6.6 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality - Cement board and sheeting. All boards and sheets must be fixed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and specifically designed for tiling.
6.7 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality - Screeds & mortar beds. Sand cement screeds must be installed as per relevant Australian Standards and left for a minimum 24 hours prior to tiling. Screeds may need longer drying time in cold climates.
6.8 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality - Tile on tile applications. Ensure all existing tiles are firmly fixed, loose or hollow tiles must be removed and the area repaired using a suitable Sika repair mortar. Existing tiles shall be adequately cleaned prior to the application of the primer. Existing tiles shall be primed with SikaTile 015 Prep n Prime and allowed to dry prior to tiling.
6.9 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality / pre-treatment. Prime substrates with a suitable Sika primer prior to adhesive application.
6.10 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Porous Substrates can be primed with.
    - SikaTile 010 Secure Prime
    - Davco Ultraprime
    - Davco PrimeX
6.11 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Non-porous substrates can be primed with.
    - SikaTile 015 Prep n Prime
6.12 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Note.
    - Refer to the spefic primer product data sheet for the complete user instructions prior to use.
    - Priming is not required directly over suitable Sika under tile waterproofing membranes.
6.13 Ecology, health and safety - Mixing. Measure the recommended amount of clean, cool potable water in a clean mixing pail, gradually add the SikaTile®-350 Pro Maxset powder while mixing with the drill until it reaches a smooth lump free trowel-able consistency. Allow the mix to stand / slake for 5 minutes then restir for an additional minute. Remix without adding additional water during the adhesives pot life.
6.14 Ecology, health and safety - Application. Tiles shall be fixed in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards.
    - Ensure the back of tiles are clean and from dust and contaminates.
    - Apply the adhesive with a notched trowel to the substrate to achieve minimum coverage requirement outlined in Australian Standards AS 3958:2023.
    - Apply the adhesive in a single direction and avoid swirls in the adhesive.
    - Apply tiles into the wet adhesive and break the adhesive notches to fully bed the tile in the adhesive layer. Ensure adequate coverage outlined in the Australian Standards is achieved to both substrate and the back of tiles.
    - Clean any residual adhesive off the face of the tile and out of the grout joints while the adhesive is still wet.
    - Expansion joints shall be installed as per relevant Australian Standards.
6.15 Ecology, health and safety - Cleaning of equipment. Tools and equipment can be cleaned with water prior to the adhesive setting. Adhesive that has set will require mechanical removal.
6.16 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.17 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
